To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the K/sup -/ meson at 2.2 BeV/c produces two hyperfragments in a single event in nuclear emulsion, and the binding energy favors the LAMBDA H/sub 4/ or the LAMBDA He/sub 4/ hyperfragments.
the K/sup -/ beam at 2,3 and 2,5 BeV/c produces events in nuclear emulsion with two hyperfragments, a meson ( K/sup +/) and a star.

we have shown that the K/sup -/ beam at 2 BeV/c produces double-hyperfragments with an average production rate of 1.5 per 10/sup 6/ incident mesons, and that the production rate of double-hyperfragment events is consistent with the assumption of a two-step production mechanism in which a hyperfragment is produced first by K/sup -/+ hyperon interaction and then the second hyperfragment is produced by the hyperon interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of hyperfragments and hypernuclei in nuclear emulsions exposed to a K/sup -/ beam at 2 Bev/c.
the development of new materials that can be used in the production of high performance, high temperature, high efficiency, high power density, and high reliability power generation systems.
a search for double hyperfragment production by K/sup -/ interaction at 2.5 and 2.3BeV/c in nuclear emulsion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of double-hyperfragments is not excluded by the evidence of this single event.
this is a very interesting event, and that it is a good example of the kind of event one expects to observe when a K- beam is incident on nuclear matter.
the data do not rule out a production mechanism of the form K/sup -/+ p/sup 4/+ He/sup 3/ + LAMBDA/sup 0/ + K/sup +/.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no significant differences between the K/sup -/ and K/sup +/ beams in the production of hyperfragments.
we have found no evidence for the existence of a new particle with a mass of about 1.5 Bev and a lifetime of about 10/sup -10/ sec. (A.E.M.)
we have found no evidence for the formation of a hypernucleus in a single event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of two hyperfragmen ts is a rare event in K/sup -/ interactions, and the production of a third particle in the final state is even more rare.
the K/sup +/ hyperfragments are not produced at a higher rate than K/sup -/ hyperfragments.
we have demonstrated that the hyperfragment production is a viable method for producing the hyperfragments in the nuclear emulsion.
